excerpts.text: Resolved to settle the matter by peaceful measures, President Jefferson in January 1803 appointed [Monroe](https://www.britannica.com/place/Monroe-county-New-York) envoy extraordinary and minister plenipotentiary to France to aid [Robert R. Livingston](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Robert-R-Livingston), the resident minister, in purchasing the territory at the mouth of the Mississippi—including the island of New Orleans—authorizing him at the same time to cooperate with [Charles Pinckney](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Charles-Pinckney), the minister at Madrid, in securing from Spain the cession of East and West Florida.

Monroe joined Livingston in Paris on April 12, after the latter’s negotiations were well under way, and the two ministers, on finding [Napoleon](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Napoleon-I) willing to dispose of the entire province of Louisiana, decided to [exceed](https://www.britannica.com/dictionary/exceed) their instructions and effect its purchase.

excerpts.text: On May 7, 1784, Jefferson was appointed by the [Congress of the Confederation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Confederation "Congress of the Confederation")[[i]](#cite_note-114) to join [Benjamin Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin "Benjamin Franklin") and [John Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Adams "John Adams") in Paris as Minister [Plenipotentiary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plenipotentiary "Plenipotentiary") for Negotiating Treaties of Amity and Commerce with [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain "Kingdom of Great Britain") and other countries.[[106]](#cite_note-115)[[j]](#cite_note-117) With his young daughter Patsy and two servants, he departed in July 1784, arriving in Paris the next month.[[108]](#cite_note-Stewart39-118)[[109]](#cite_note-119) Jefferson had Patsy educated at [Pentemont Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentemont_Abbey "Pentemont Abbey"). Less than a year later, he was assigned the additional duty of succeeding Franklin as Minister to France.
